video.title: Southborough K-8 School Committee, Special Open meeting January 9, 2026

summary.headline: School Committee reviewed the revised FY27 budget and voted to advance districtwide technology and security upgrades into the FY27 capital plan.
summary.summary: The Southborough School Committee met in a special session to review revisions to the proposed FY27 operating budget, which stands at a 3.67 percent increase over FY26. Members evaluated cost offsets, recommending keeping emergency facility maintenance funds in the operational budget and reducing reliance on circuit breaker reserves to prevent future deficits. The committee also voted unanimously to accelerate districtwide security system upgrades and classroom display technology into the FY27 capital plan for town consideration.

topics.title: FY27 operating budget review and discussion
topics.summary: The superintendent presented a revised preliminary operating budget reflecting a 3.67 percent increase over FY26, reduced from an earlier 5.78 percent estimate. The budget maintains level services but excludes a planned third world language teacher, an instructional technology specialist, and a restored library position. Committee members advised against offsetting operating costs with facility revolving funds and recommended lowering an aggressive $500,000 circuit breaker reserve drawdown to roughly $350,000 to avoid creating a severe structural deficit in FY28.
key_details: Fixed special education costs rose by approximately $700,000 across out-of-district tuition, collaborative tuition, and transportation.
Foregoing the third world language teacher saves roughly $100,000 (about 0.4 percent of the budget) and shifts Spanish instruction to grades 1 through 5, removing it from kindergarten.
The committee favored reducing the proposed $500,000 circuit breaker offset down to $350,000 to protect future budgets.
Members opposed using $45,000 from the facilities revolving fund for routine maintenance, reserving it instead for building emergencies like mold or heating failures.
The administration will update the figures and present the recommended budget at the regular meeting on January 14.
topics.outcome: Guidance provided to administration to adjust offsets and prepare the presentation for the upcoming meeting.
topics.why_it_matters: The operating budget directly impacts the town tax levy, school staffing levels, and elementary school curriculum offerings.

topics.title: FY27 facilities capital plan and project adjustments
topics.summary: The committee reviewed the 10-year facilities capital plan, focusing on projects scheduled for FY27. Discussions centered on whether to spread technology and security improvements over multiple years or bundle them into FY27 to achieve economies of scale and seek town capital bonding. Members agreed all schools, including Neary Elementary regardless of the outcome of its upcoming March project vote, should receive equitable and immediate security and technology upgrades.
key_details: Capital projects slated for FY27 include $810,000 for flooring at Finn School and a $1.8 million roof replacement at Trottier Middle School.
The committee favored bundling all interactive classroom smartboard upgrades across grades K-8 into FY27 rather than phasing them over multiple years.
Security system upgrades across district schools were also accelerated into FY27 to ensure equal safety protections at all buildings.
Administration will coordinate with town capital committees regarding potential bonding strategies.
Potential risks from federal grant reductions under Title I through IV and IDEA were also noted.
topics.outcome: Approved two motions consolidating technology infrastructure and security upgrades into FY27.
topics.why_it_matters: Bundling large capital investments into FY27 shapes future town meeting warrant articles, borrowing authorizations, and school facility safety.

votes.motion: Approve moving all out-years for technology infrastructure and equipment to FY27 in the capital plan.
Approve moving all out-years for security system upgrades to FY27 in the capital plan.
